This study provides specific LC-MS/MS analytical parameters for quantifying adenosine and inosine in murine tumor tissues, including column type (ZORBAX RRHD Eclipse Plus C18), mobile phase gradients (water/acetonitrile with 0.1% FA), flow rate (300 µL min⁻¹), and MRM transitions (inosine 269.1/136.8, adenosine 268.1/135.9). It also describes a solid-phase microextraction (SPME) technique for measuring free metabolite concentrations in the tumor microenvironment using HLB-PAN fibers and kinetic calibration. A baseline adenosine concentration of 0.04 µM is reported for control mouse tumors.

This study provides a detailed methodological framework for serum metabolite quantification using gas-chromatography/mass-spectrometry (GC/MS), which offers supporting technical parameters for the requested gap. The authors specify sample processing standards including serum separation (3,000 x g, 10 min, 4°C), storage conditions (−80°C), and extraction protocols (MeOH:H2O:CHCl3 = 2.5:1:1 with 2-isopropylmalic acid internal standard). The study outlines specific GC/MS instrument parameters such as column type (CP-SIL 8 CB), temperature programming (80°C to 330°C), and ion-source settings (200°C), along with quality control measures like calculating relative standard deviation (RSD%) and evaluating intra-day/inter-day variance. While the specific metabolites quantified (2-hydroxybutyrate, aspartic acid, kynurenine, cystamine) do not match the gap's target (inosine or short-chain fatty acids), the documented workflow serves as a reference template for establishing absolute physiological concentration protocols in human serum. The authors also demonstrate how to establish reference concentration ranges and cut-off values for cancer patients versus healthy controls using logistic regression and ROC analysis, providing a statistical model for defining cancer-specific reference ranges even though the specific analytes differ.

content: Targeted LC-MS/MS parameters for inosine quantification in human serum: Kinetex HILIC column (150 × 3 mm, 2.6 μm), isocratic elution (0.2% formic acid in water:methanol 10:90), flow rate 0.25 mL/min, column temp 50 °C, negative ionization mode, MRM transitions monitored (specific transitions listed in Supplementary Table S1 of the study).
relevance: Directly addresses success criterion (1) for analytical platform parameters for inosine.

content: Sample processing standards for serum metabolites: Blood collected in clotting activator tubes, sera aliquoted and stored at −80 °C, thawed on ice, protein precipitation using ice-cold methanol (350 µL to 100 µL serum), vortexed and centrifuged (13,000g, 10 min, 4 °C).
relevance: Directly addresses success criterion (2) for sample processing standards (extraction, storage).

content: Absolute concentration ranges for inosine in cancer patients: Lung Cancer (LC) group mean 5.88 μM (median 5.38 μM) in discovery set; mean 5.54 μM (median 3.72 μM) in validation set. COPD control group mean 2.36 μM (median 1.15 μM) in discovery set.
relevance: Directly addresses success criterion (3) for reference concentration ranges in cancer patients, though controls are disease-matched (COPD) rather than healthy.

content: Targeted LC-MS/MS parameters for succinic acid quantification: Same HILIC method as inosine, negative ionization mode, validated according to EMA guidelines with LOQ, precision (CV < 13.8%), and accuracy (%bias < 14.8%) reported.
relevance: Provides protocol for succinic acid, a TCA cycle intermediate often analyzed alongside SCFAs, though chemically distinct from microbiome-derived SCFAs (acetate/propionate/butyrate).
